final_text:
Recursion is when a function calls itself on a smaller version of the same problem.

Every recursive function needs a base case — a version of the problem small enough to answer outright — otherwise it never stops.

The classic example is factorial: `n! = n * (n-1)!`, with `0! = 1` as the base case.
